entities.name: Malaria
entities.description: Life-threatening protozoan intraerythrocytic parasitic infection caused by Plasmodium species, characterized by cyclical fever paroxysms, acute hemolysis, profound thrombocytopenia, and risk of microvascular sequestration or multiorgan failure.

entities.name: Uncomplicated Malaria
entities.description: Acute febrile presentation lacking vital organ dysfunction, with fever, chills, diaphoresis, headache, and myalgias.

entities.name: Severe Falciparum Malaria
entities.description: Medical emergency caused by Plasmodium falciparum with high parasitemia, microvascular cytoadherence, and multiorgan failure.

entities.name: Cerebral Malaria
entities.description: Severe neurological complication characterized by unarousable coma, encephalopathy, and generalized seizures.

entities.name: Blackwater Fever
entities.description: Syndrome of massive intravascular hemolysis producing dark mahogany hemoglobinuria and acute renal failure.

entities.name: Acute Kidney Injury
entities.description: Abrupt decline in renal excretory function with oliguria and serum creatinine elevation above 3.0 mg/dL.

entities.name: Severe Malarial Anemia
entities.description: Critical hematologic failure with hemoglobin below 5 g/dL in children or below 7 g/dL in adults.

entities.name: Non-Cardiogenic Pulmonary Edema
entities.description: Severe respiratory compromise with alveolar capillary leak and bilateral infiltrates without left heart failure.

entities.name: Acute Respiratory Distress
entities.description: Severe tachypnea, intercostal retractions, and deep labored breathing reflecting lung injury or acidosis.

entities.name: Profound Hypoglycemia
entities.description: Blood glucose below 2.2 mmol/L (40 mg/dL) causing diaphoresis, tachycardia, and altered consciousness.

entities.name: Lactic Acidosis
entities.description: Metabolic acidosis with plasma lactate above 5 mmol/L and base deficit exceeding 10 mEq/L.

entities.name: Algid Malaria
entities.description: Decompensated circulatory shock with profound hypotension, hypothermia, and peripheral circulatory collapse.

entities.name: Circulatory Collapse
entities.description: Hemodynamic failure with cold clammy extremities, core-to-skin temperature gradient, and prolonged capillary refill.

entities.name: Malarial Retinopathy
entities.description: Specific funduscopic triad of retinal whitening, vessel discoloration, and retinal hemorrhages.

entities.name: Spontaneous Bleeding Diathesis
entities.description: Systemic or mucocutaneous hemorrhage including epistaxis, gastrointestinal bleeding, and venipuncture oozing.

entities.name: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation
entities.description: Consumptive coagulopathy with prolonged PT/aPTT, hypofibrinogenemia, and elevated D-dimer in severe malaria.

entities.name: Malarial Hyperpyrexia
entities.description: Core body temperature exceeding 40°C (104°F) causing delirium, tachypnea, and febrile seizures.

entities.name: Post-Malaria Neurological Syndrome
entities.description: Self-limiting acute neuropsychiatric or encephalopathic syndrome developing after parasite clearance.

entities.name: Hyperreactive Malarial Splenomegaly
entities.description: Chronic immunological disorder featuring massive splenomegaly, polyclonal IgM elevation, and hypersplenism.

entities.name: Splenic Rupture
entities.description: Catastrophic tear of an acutely congested, friable spleen presenting with hemoperitoneum and shock.

entities.name: Splenic Infarction
entities.description: Ischemic necrosis of splenic tissue resulting from microvascular congestion and parasitized cell sequestration.

entities.name: Malarial Hepatopathy
entities.description: Severe hepatic dysfunction featuring deep jaundice, mild-to-moderate transaminitis, and Kupffer hyperplasia.

entities.name: Placental Malaria
entities.description: Sequestration of VAR2CSA-expressing parasitized erythrocytes in the maternal placental intervillous space.

entities.name: Low Birth Weight
entities.description: Neonatal birth weight below 2,500 grams resulting from chronic placental malarial insufficiency.

entities.name: Preterm Delivery
entities.description: Spontaneous labor before 37 weeks gestation triggered by acute febrile paroxysms and maternal cytokines.

entities.name: Congenital Malaria
entities.description: Transplacental transmission of Plasmodium asexual stages to the neonate, causing fever and anemia.

entities.name: Severe Vivax Malaria
entities.description: Complicated Plasmodium vivax infection with severe anemia, pulmonary edema, and circulatory shock.

entities.name: Vivax Splenic Rupture
entities.description: Atraumatic rupture of the splenic capsule in vivax malaria due to rapid hyperplasia and reticulocyte trapping.

entities.name: Severe Knowlesi Malaria
entities.description: Fulminant simian zoonotic malaria characterized by hyperparasitemia, acute renal failure, and jaundice.

entities.name: Daily Quotidian Fever
entities.description: Fever spikes recurring every 24 hours corresponding to synchronous 24-hour schizogony in P. knowlesi.

entities.name: Quartan Malarial Nephropathy
entities.description: Chronic immune-complex glomerulonephritis and steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome in P. malariae infection.

entities.name: Immune Complex Glomerulonephritis
entities.description: Glomerular inflammation mediated by subendothelial deposition of parasite antigens and immune complexes.

entities.name: Generalized Convulsions
entities.description: Recurrent tonic-clonic seizure episodes occurring during cerebral sequestration or hyperpyrexia.

entities.name: Unarousable Coma
entities.description: Deep state of unconsciousness unresponsive to noxious stimuli, defining cerebral malaria.

entities.name: Prostration
entities.description: Extreme physical weakness rendering the patient unable to sit unsupported, stand, or walk.

entities.name: Acidotic Kussmaul Breathing
entities.description: Deep, rapid, labored respirations without airway obstruction, compensating for metabolic acidosis.

entities.name: Persistent Vomiting
entities.description: Intractable emesis precluding oral fluid and medication intake, necessitating parenteral antimalarials.

entities.name: Macroscopic Hemoglobinuria
entities.description: Excretion of dark red, burgundy, or black urine resulting from massive intravascular erythrocyte lysis.

entities.name: Malarial Hemoglobinuric Nephrosis
entities.description: Toxic acute tubular necrosis provoked by heme cast deposition and lipid peroxidation in renal tubules.

entities.name: Microvascular Erythrocyte Sequestration
entities.description: Cytoadherence of mature trophozoite-infected red cells to capillary endothelial receptors causing ischemia.

entities.name: Secondary Bacterial Bacteremia
entities.description: Co-infection with invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella or enteric bacilli due to gut ischemia.

entities.name: Classic Malarial Paroxysm
entities.description: Pathognomonic triphasic sequence of shaking rigors, blazing hyperthermia, and drenching diaphoresis.

entities.name: Paroxysm Cold Stage
entities.description: Initial 15-60 minute phase of violent teeth-chattering rigors, piloerection, and peripheral cyanosis.

entities.name: Paroxysm Hot Stage
entities.description: Second 2-6 hour phase of burning dry skin, hyperpyrexia (39-41°C), and severe throbbing cephalalgia.

entities.name: Paroxysm Sweating Stage
entities.description: Concluding 2-4 hour phase of profuse drenching diaphoresis, rapid defervescence, and exhaustion.

entities.name: Tertian Fever Periodicity
entities.description: Fever paroxysms recurring every 48 hours in P. vivax, P. ovale, and synchronized P. falciparum.

entities.name: Quartan Fever Periodicity
entities.description: Fever paroxysms recurring strictly every 72 hours matching the 72-hour cycle of P. malariae.

entities.name: Quotidian Fever Periodicity
entities.description: Fever paroxysms recurring every 24 hours corresponding to the 24-hour cycle of P. knowlesi.

entities.name: Tender Splenomegaly
entities.description: Acute palpable enlargement of the spleen tender to palpation, appearing within 3-7 days of onset.

entities.name: Soft Splenomegaly
entities.description: Soft, easily compressible consistency of the acutely enlarged spleen on physical examination.

entities.name: Scleral Icterus
entities.description: Yellow discoloration of sclerae reflecting elevated indirect bilirubin from active erythrocyte hemolysis.

entities.name: Mucocutaneous Pallor
entities.description: Noticeable paleness of skin and mucous membranes indicating acute hemolytic anemia.

entities.name: Palmar Pallor
entities.description: Paleness of palmar skin and creases indicating severe anemia in pediatric triage.

entities.name: Conjunctival Pallor
entities.description: Marked pallor of the inferior palpebral conjunctiva signifying hemoglobin below 7-8 g/dL.

entities.name: Retinal Whitening
entities.description: Patchy, pale opacification of the macula or peripheral retina from capillary sequestration.

entities.name: Retinal Vessel Discoloration
entities.description: Abnormal orange or white appearance of retinal capillaries due to sequestered parasites.

entities.name: Retinal Blot Hemorrhages
entities.description: Scattered flame and blot hemorrhages across the posterior pole on funduscopic exam.

entities.name: Roth Spots
entities.description: Pale-centered intraretinal hemorrhages caused by localized capillary thrombosis.

entities.name: Blantyre Score Below 3
entities.description: Pediatric coma score under 3 out of 5 confirming unarousable coma in cerebral malaria.

entities.name: Low Glasgow Coma Score
entities.description: Adult Glasgow Coma Scale score under 11 indicating severe cerebral dysfunction.

entities.name: Hyperpyrexia Over 40C
entities.description: Extreme core elevation exceeding 40°C on clinical thermometry during febrile peaks.

entities.name: Tender Hepatomegaly
entities.description: Palpable, tender liver edge 2-4 cm below right costal margin from acute congestion.

entities.name: Peripheral Vasoconstriction
entities.description: Intense cutis anserina and acral cyanosis occurring during the shivering paroxysm.

entities.name: Cold Clammy Extremities
entities.description: Cool, moist distal extremities indicating algid shock and severe peripheral shut-down.

entities.name: Prolonged Capillary Refill
entities.description: Delayed capillary refill exceeding 3 seconds indicating impaired systemic microcirculation.

entities.name: Acidotic Hyperventilation
entities.description: Deep, unlabored rapid respiration without lung crackles driven by metabolic acidosis.

entities.name: Bibasilar Pulmonary Crackles
entities.description: Fine end-inspiratory crackles auscultated over lung bases indicating alveolar transudation.

entities.name: Postural Hypotension
entities.description: Orthostatic blood pressure decrease with postural tachycardia from fever and dehydration.

entities.name: Absence of Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Complete lack of significant localized or generalized peripheral lymph node enlargement.

entities.name: Thick Blood Smear
entities.description: Concentrated dehemoglobinized blood film for sensitive parasite detection down to 10 parasites/µL.

entities.name: Thin Blood Smear
entities.description: Methanol-fixed monolayer blood smear allowing species identification and parasitemia counting.

entities.name: Intraerythrocytic Ring Forms
entities.description: Delicate trophozoite rings with blue cytoplasm and red chromatin dot inside erythrocytes.

entities.name: Falciparum Gametocytes
entities.description: Diagnostic crescent- or banana-shaped sexual stages characteristic of Plasmodium falciparum.

entities.name: Amoeboid Trophozoites
entities.description: Irregular, spread-out trophozoite forms within enlarged erythrocytes in P. vivax infection.

entities.name: Schüffner Dots
entities.description: Fine red/pink cytoplasmic stippling throughout parasitized erythrocytes in vivax and ovale.

entities.name: Malariae Band Forms
entities.description: Equatorial ribbon-like trophozoite bands stretching across senescent erythrocytes in P. malariae.

entities.name: Knowlesi Band Forms
entities.description: Microscopic band forms mimicking P. malariae but accompanied by dense falciparum-like ring load.

entities.name: PfHRP2 Antigen Positivity
entities.description: Rapid immunochromatographic detection of P. falciparum histidine-rich protein 2.

entities.name: Pan-pLDH Antigen Positivity
entities.description: Positive parasite lactate dehydrogenase assay reflecting active metabolic turnover across all species.

entities.name: Aldolase Antigen Positivity
entities.description: Positive pan-Plasmodium aldolase glycolytic enzyme assay on combination RDT cassettes.

entities.name: HRP2 Gene Deletion
entities.description: Chromosomal deletion of pfhrp2/pfhrp3 genes producing false-negative PfHRP2 RDT results.

entities.name: Unconjugated Hyperbilirubinemia
entities.description: Elevation of indirect bilirubin (> 2.0 mg/dL) reflecting brisk erythrocyte hemolysis.

entities.name: Depleted Serum Haptoglobin
entities.description: Undetectable haptoglobin (< 0.1 g/L) secondary to binding of free intravascular hemoglobin.

entities.name: Elevated Lactate Dehydrogenase
entities.description: Marked elevation of serum LDH (> 500-1500 IU/L) tracking active red blood cell destruction.

entities.name: Marked Thrombocytopenia
entities.description: Platelet count depressed below 100,000/µL in 70-85% of acute malaria presentations.

entities.name: Profound Thrombocytopenia
entities.description: Platelet count dropping below 50,000/µL due to splenic sequestration and immune clearance.

entities.name: Normal Leukocyte Count
entities.description: Normal WBC count (4,000-10,000/µL) differentiating malaria from acute bacterial sepsis.

entities.name: Leukopenia
entities.description: Absolute white cell count below 4,000/µL during acute fever peaks from splenic margination.

entities.name: Hyperparasitemia Over Two Percent
entities.description: Parasitemia exceeding 2% infected red cells denoting severe disease in non-immune travelers.

entities.name: Hyperparasitemia Over Ten Percent
entities.description: Parasitemia exceeding 10% infected erythrocytes defining severe malaria regardless of immunity.

entities.name: Parasitemia Over 100000
entities.description: Absolute asexual parasite count exceeding 100,000/µL indicating heavy microvascular parasite burden.

entities.name: Elevated Plasma Lactate
entities.description: Venous or arterial lactate exceeding 5.0 mmol/L reflecting widespread tissue hypoperfusion.

entities.name: Elevated Base Deficit
entities.description: Base deficit exceeding 10 mEq/L on blood gas analysis identifying severe metabolic exhaustion.

entities.name: Low Serum Bicarbonate
entities.description: Serum bicarbonate below 15 mmol/L consumed by organic lactic acid accumulation.

entities.name: Profound Hypoglycemia Level
entities.description: Blood glucose below 2.2 mmol/L (40 mg/dL) recorded on bedside glucometer or lab testing.

entities.name: Elevated Serum Creatinine
entities.description: Serum creatinine rising above 3.0 mg/dL (265 µmol/L) indicating acute renal dysfunction.

entities.name: Elevated Blood Urea
entities.description: Blood urea nitrogen elevation exceeding 20 mmol/L from tissue breakdown and reduced clearance.

entities.name: Dark Mahogany Urine
entities.description: Visual appearance of urine resembling black tea, port-wine, or dark mahogany in blackwater fever.

entities.name: Hemoglobinuria Without Erythrocyturia
entities.description: Urine dipstick strongly positive for blood with complete absence of intact red cells on sediment.

entities.name: Normocytic Normochromic Anemia
entities.description: Acute drop in hemoglobin and hematocrit with normal MCV and MCHC on complete blood count.

entities.name: Compensatory Reticulocytosis
entities.description: Elevated reticulocyte production index (> 2.0%) appearing several days following the hemolytic episode.

entities.name: Mild Transaminase Elevation
entities.description: Modest elevation of AST and ALT (1.5 to 3 times upper limit of normal) without liver necrosis.

entities.name: Absence of Overt DIC
entities.description: Normal prothrombin time and normal fibrinogen levels despite marked thrombocytopenia.

entities.name: POCUS Splenomegaly
entities.description: Bedside ultrasound confirmation of splenic bipolar length exceeding 12 cm with homogeneous texture.

entities.name: POCUS Normal Gallbladder
entities.description: Thin gallbladder wall under 3 mm on bedside ultrasound without pericholecystic fluid.

entities.name: POCUS Absent Leakage
entities.description: Absence of ascites, pleural effusions, or pericardial fluid on rapid bedside sonography.

entities.name: Chest Radiograph Clear Lungs
entities.description: Initial clear chest radiograph without consolidation or effusions in uncomplicated cases.

entities.name: Anopheles Mosquito Bite
entities.description: Inoculation of infectious sporozoites by female mosquitoes of the genus Anopheles during blood feeding.

entities.name: Nocturnal Vector Biting
entities.description: Exposure to mosquito biting activity between dusk and dawn, the peak foraging window of Anopheles vectors.

entities.name: Tropical Endemic Travel
entities.description: Recent travel to or residence in malaria-endemic tropical and subtropical latitudes.

entities.name: Sub-Saharan Africa Travel
entities.description: Travel history to sub-Saharan Africa, which harbors >95% of worldwide malaria mortality.

entities.name: Southeast Asia Travel
entities.description: Travel to forested or border areas of Southeast Asia where P. vivax and zoonotic P. knowlesi circulate.

entities.name: Amazon Basin Travel
entities.description: Travel within South American rainforest basins where Plasmodium vivax is responsible for most infections.

entities.name: Lack of Chemoprophylaxis
entities.description: Failure to take recommended antimalarial chemoprophylaxis regimens during high-risk exposure.

entities.name: Non-Immune Traveler
entities.description: Travelers and migrants lacking pre-existing semi-immune antibody protection against malaria.

entities.name: Children Under Five
entities.description: Young children with naive immunity carrying approximately 75% of global malaria deaths.

entities.name: Pregnant Women
entities.description: Expectant mothers with altered systemic immunity and placental chondroitin sulfate A sequestration.

entities.name: HIV Co-Infection
entities.description: Patients with HIV/AIDS who have impaired cell-mediated control and higher parasite burdens.

entities.name: Asplenic Patients
entities.description: Individuals with surgical asplenia or hyposplenism lacking mechanical splenic parasite clearance.

entities.name: Contaminated Blood Transfusion
entities.description: Direct transmission of intraerythrocytic parasites via donor blood units bypassing liver schizogony.

entities.name: Contaminated Needle Sharing
entities.description: Direct bloodborne inoculation through shared hypodermic needles among intravenous drug users.

entities.name: Congenital Inoculation
entities.description: Vertical transplacental transmission of asexual parasites from infected mother to fetus.

entities.name: Falciparum Incubation Period
entities.description: Incubation period of 9 to 14 days (typically 10-12 days) for Plasmodium falciparum infections.

entities.name: Falciparum Minimum Incubation
entities.description: Biological minimum liver schizogony threshold of 7 days before falciparum enters bloodstream.

entities.name: Vivax Primary Incubation
entities.description: Primary incubation period of 12 to 18 days for initial attacks of Plasmodium vivax and ovale.

entities.name: Vivax Delayed Latency
entities.description: Prolonged incubation or latency of 8 to 10 months seen in temperate strains of P. vivax.

entities.name: Dormant Liver Hypnozoites
entities.description: Quiescent intrahepatic stages of P. vivax and P. ovale capable of reactivation and late relapse.

entities.name: Ovale Incubation Period
entities.description: Incubation period of 15 to 18 days for Plasmodium ovale before initial paroxysms emerge.

entities.name: Malariae Extended Incubation
entities.description: Prolonged incubation period of 18 to 40 days for Plasmodium malariae with chronic persistence.

entities.name: Knowlesi Incubation Period
entities.description: Incubation period of 9 to 12 days following transmission of zoonotic simian knowlesi parasites.

entities.name: Urban Anopheles Stephensi
entities.description: Invasive mosquito vector breeding in man-made clean water containers in African and Asian cities.

entities.name: Serial Negative Blood Smears
entities.description: Three negative quality-assured thick and thin Giemsa smears taken 12-24 hours apart.

entities.name: Onset Under Seven Days
entities.description: Fever onset occurring within less than 7 days of entering an endemic transmission area.

entities.name: Microvascular Plasma Leakage
entities.description: Significant capillary hyperpermeability with hemoconcentration (hematocrit rise >= 20%) or ascites.

entities.name: Marked Neutrophilic Leukocytosis
entities.description: White blood cell count exceeding 15,000/µL with bandemia and toxic granulations.

entities.name: Cutaneous Necrotic Eschar
entities.description: Black necrotic cigarette-burn ulcer with erythematous halo pathognomonic of scrub typhus.

entities.name: Prominent Regional Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Noticeable tender localized lymph node enlargement draining an inoculation site.

entities.name: Diffuse Maculopapular Rash
entities.description: Widespread erythematous maculopapular or petechial exanthem covering trunk and extremities.

entities.name: Transaminases Over 1000 UL
entities.description: Massive transaminase elevation exceeding 1,000 U/L indicating acute viral or toxic hepatitis.

entities.name: Bilateral Conjunctival Suffusion
entities.description: Marked bilateral ciliary injection without exudate characteristic of leptospirosis.

entities.name: Dense Lobar Consolidation
entities.description: Focal dense radiographic consolidation with air bronchograms confirming bacterial pneumonia.

entities.name: Purulent Cerebrospinal Fluid
entities.description: Turbid CSF with neutrophil-predominant pleocytosis (> 100 WBC/µL) and low glucose.

entities.name: Exudative Tonsillitis
entities.description: Confluent tonsillopharyngeal exudates and anterior cervical lymphadenitis.

entities.name: Pyuria With Bacteriuria
entities.description: Urinary sediment showing > 10 leukocytes per high-power field and visible bacterial rods.

entities.name: Acute Surgical Peritonitis
entities.description: Board-like abdominal rigidity and involuntary guarding from hollow visceral perforation.

entities.name: Direct Hyperbilirubinemia Predominance
entities.description: Conjugated bilirubin exceeding 50% of total bilirubin with elevated alkaline phosphatase.

entities.name: Acholic Pale Stools
entities.description: Clay-colored stools reflecting complete mechanical biliary duct obstruction.

entities.name: Continuous Stepladder Fever
entities.description: Gradual daily temperature escalation accompanied by relative bradycardia (Faget sign).

entities.name: Beta-Lactam Monotherapy Response
entities.description: Rapid complete fever defervescence upon administration of penicillins or cephalosporins.

entities.name: Absence of Endemic Exposure
entities.description: Complete lack of travel to malaria-endemic zones and no bloodborne exposures.

entities.name: Normal Platelet Count
entities.description: Persistently normal platelet count (> 200,000/µL) across serial complete blood counts.

entities.name: Severe Hypofibrinogenemia
entities.description: Fibrinogen dropping below 100 mg/dL with prolonged clotting times on admission.

entities.name: Splenic Abscess
entities.description: Focal cystic splenic cavity with internal echoes and wall enhancement on ultrasound.

entities.name: Dengue Fever
entities.description: Arboviral illness presenting with retro-orbital headache, rash, hemoconcentration, and plasma leak.

entities.name: Typhoid Fever
entities.description: Enteric fever caused by Salmonella Typhi with stepladder fever, bradycardia, and rose spots.

entities.name: Leptospirosis
entities.description: Zoonotic spirochetal illness causing conjunctival suffusion, severe calf pain, and renal failure.

entities.name: Scrub Typhus
entities.description: Chigger-borne infection by Orientia tsutsugamushi causing an eschar, adenopathy, and maculopapular rash.

entities.name: Babesiosis
entities.description: Tick-borne intraerythrocytic protozoan causing fever, hemolysis, and pathognomonic Maltese cross tetrads.

entities.name: African Trypanosomiasis
entities.description: Protozoan disease transmitted by tsetse flies presenting with chancre, Winterbottom sign, and somnolence.

entities.name: Visceral Leishmaniasis
entities.description: Chronic protozoan infection causing protracted fever, massive firm splenomegaly, and pancytopenia.

entities.name: Yellow Fever
entities.description: Flavivirus infection presenting with biphasic fever, profound hepatocellular jaundice, and hematemesis.

entities.name: Acute Viral Hepatitis
entities.description: Acute hepatocellular necrosis with transaminases > 1,000 U/L, direct jaundice, and dark urine.

entities.name: Meningococcal Meningitis
entities.description: Acute bacterial leptomeningitis featuring neck stiffness, purpuric rash, and purulent CSF.

entities.name: Bacterial Sepsis
entities.description: Systemic pyogenic bacteremia with marked neutrophilia, high procalcitonin, and focal source.

entities.name: Influenza Infection
entities.description: Acute respiratory viral infection with dry cough, sore throat, coryza, and myalgias.

entities.name: Chikungunya Virus
entities.description: Arboviral illness causing crippling symmetrical small joint polyarthritis and rash.

entities.name: Relapsing Fever Borreliosis
entities.description: Spirochetal infection by Borrelia recurrentis causing prolonged recurring fevers and spirochetemia.

entities.name: Q Fever
entities.description: Zoonotic infection by Coxiella burnetii presenting with atypical pneumonia or hepatitis.

entities.name: Acute HIV Seroconversion
entities.description: Mononucleosis-like illness with generalized adenopathy, mucosal ulcers, and morbilliform rash.

entities.name: Human Granulocytic Anaplasmosis
entities.description: Tick-borne rickettsial illness with intracytoplasmic neutrophil morulae responsive to doxycycline.

entities.name: Amebic Liver Abscess
entities.description: Extra-intestinal amebiasis causing right upper quadrant pain, intercostal tenderness, and hepatic cavity.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, uncomplicated malaria, acute febrile illness, constitutional symptoms, chills
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Presents in non-immune or semi-immune individuals as uncomplicated malaria characterized by constitutional symptoms including intermittent fever, rigors, cephalalgia, generalized arthromyalgia, anorexia, and abdominal discomfort without vital organ compromise.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, severe malaria, falciparum, organ dysfunction, hyperparasitemia, vital organ failure
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as severe falciparum malaria when microvascular sequestration and an intense inflammatory cascade precipitate life-threatening complications such as cerebral malaria, severe metabolic acidosis, acute renal failure, and respiratory failure.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, cerebral malaria, unarousable coma, encephalopathy, seizures, retinopathy
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as cerebral malaria through extensive microvascular sequestration of parasitized erythrocytes in cerebral capillaries, producing unarousable coma, generalized convulsions, intracranial hypertension, and malarial retinopathy.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, blackwater fever, intravascular hemolysis, hemoglobinuria, acute tubular necrosis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as blackwater fever marked by acute, overwhelming intravascular erythrocyte destruction producing dark red to mahogany-black urine saturated with free hemoglobin, severe prostration, and acute tubular necrosis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, acute kidney injury, renal failure, oliguria, elevated creatinine, hemoglobin casts
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as acute kidney injury resulting from renal tubular obstruction by hemoglobin casts, microvascular sequestration of parasitized erythrocytes, and systemic hypoperfusion, predominantly in adult patients.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, severe anemia, profound pallor, hemolysis, dyserythropoiesis, transfusion requirement
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as severe malarial anemia resulting from accelerated splenic destruction of parasitized and non-parasitized erythrocytes combined with cytokine-mediated suppression of erythropoiesis, demanding urgent blood transfusion.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, pulmonary edema, ARDS, capillary leak, fluid overload, respiratory failure
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) triggered by systemic endothelial activation and alveolar capillary leakage, frequently aggravated by vigorous fluid resuscitation.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, respiratory distress, tachypnea, retractions, metabolic acidosis, hypoxemia
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as acute respiratory distress evidenced by rapid, labored breathing, intercostal indrawing, and oxygen desaturation, functioning as an essential herald of severe lactic acidosis or pulmonary capillary damage.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, hypoglycemia, neuroglycopenia, impaired gluconeogenesis, hyperinsulinemia, quinine
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as profound hypoglycemia secondary to parasite glucose consumption, impaired hepatic gluconeogenesis, and hyperinsulinemia induced by pancreatic beta-cell stimulation during parenteral quinine administration.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, lactic acidosis, metabolic acidosis, tissue hypoxia, lactate, base deficit
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as systemic lactic acidosis driven by microvascular erythrocyte sequestration, tissue hypoperfusion, anaerobic glycolysis in underperfused capillary beds, and direct parasite metabolic lactate generation.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, algid malaria, septic shock, hypotension, peripheral collapse, bacteremia
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as algid malaria presenting with profound systemic hypotension, peripheral vasoconstriction, weak thready pulse, and circulatory collapse, frequently complicated by concurrent Gram-negative bacteremia.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, circulatory collapse, shock, vasoconstriction, capillary refill, hypoperfusion
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as circulatory collapse secondary to severe microvascular obstruction, myocardial depression, and severe metabolic acidosis, requiring urgent inotropic and vasopressor hemodynamic support.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, malarial retinopathy, retinal whitening, vessel discoloration, retinal hemorrhages
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as malarial retinopathy on funduscopic examination, providing direct bedside visualization of microvascular capillary sequestration, blood-retinal barrier breakdown, and tissue hypoxia.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, bleeding diathesis, mucosal hemorrhage, epistaxis, coagulopathy, thrombocytopenia
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as spontaneous bleeding diathesis characterized by recurrent epistaxis, petechiae, or gastrointestinal hemorrhage, resulting from profound thrombocytopenia combined with consumption of clotting factors.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, disseminated intravascular coagulation, DIC, consumptive coagulopathy, thrombosis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) in hyperparasitemic or septic cases, leading to widespread microvascular thrombosis and secondary consumable coagulopathy.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, malarial hyperpyrexia, hyperthermia, extreme fever, febrile delirium, rigors
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as malarial hyperpyrexia with sustained axillary or rectal temperatures above 40°C driven by massive pyrogen release during schizont rupture, demanding aggressive active antipyresis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, post-malaria neurological syndrome, PMNS, post-infectious encephalitis, psychosis, ataxia
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as post-malaria neurological syndrome presenting with acute psychosis, tremors, ataxia, or generalized seizures weeks after successful parasite clearance, believed to be an immune-mediated post-infectious encephalitis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, hyperreactive malarial splenomegaly, tropical splenomegaly syndrome, IgM, hypersplenism
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as hyperreactive malarial splenomegaly characterized by huge painless splenomegaly crossing the midline, pronounced polyclonal IgM hypergammaglobulinemia, hypersplenic cytopenias, and high antimalarial antibody titers.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, splenic rupture, hemoperitoneum, left upper quadrant pain, Kehr sign, surgical abdomen
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as acute spontaneous splenic rupture presenting with sudden left upper quadrant peritonism, Kehr sign (referred left shoulder pain), and hemoperitoneum-induced hemorrhagic shock.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, splenic infarction, ischemic necrosis, left hypochondrial pain, splenic friction rub
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as splenic infarction presenting with acute focal pleuritic left upper quadrant pain, friction rub over the splenic bed, and wedge-shaped hypodense lesions on abdominal ultrasound.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, malarial hepatopathy, jaundice, hepatic dysfunction, transaminitis, Kupffer cells
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as malarial hepatopathy featuring prominent clinical jaundice, tender hepatomegaly, and impaired hepatic synthetic function secondary to microvascular Kupffer cell hyperplasia and centrilobular ischemic injury.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, placental malaria, pregnancy, VAR2CSA, intervillous space, maternal anemia
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as placental malaria where VAR2CSA-expressing P. falciparum parasites selectively sequester within the maternal placental intervillous space, compromising fetal-maternal nutrient exchange.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, low birth weight, intrauterine growth restriction, infant mortality, pregnancy malaria
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as low birth weight in newborns of mothers infected during pregnancy, constituting a leading cause of neonatal and infant mortality across high-transmission settings.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, preterm delivery, miscarriage, premature labor, pregnancy complication
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as preterm delivery and miscarriage in pregnant women experiencing high fever spikes and acute severe malaria during pregnancy.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, congenital malaria, vertical transmission, neonatal fever, hepatosplenomegaly
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as congenital malaria in infants presenting within the first few weeks of life with poor feeding, irritability, fever, pallor, and detectable circulating parasitemia.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, severe vivax malaria, pulmonary edema, severe anemia, vivax shock, acute lung injury
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as severe vivax malaria manifesting with profound anemia, acute lung injury, splenic rupture, and systemic inflammatory collapse despite lower circulating parasitemia.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, vivax splenic rupture, splenic capsule tear, acute hemoperitoneum, vivax complication
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as vivax splenic rupture when acute expansion and reticulocyte-rich congestion of the red pulp cause sudden subcapsular hemorrhage and peritoneal extravasation.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, severe knowlesi malaria, zoonotic malaria, hyperparasitemia, hepatorenal failure
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as severe knowlesi malaria marked by an explosive 24-hour replication cycle that causes acute renal failure, jaundice, ARDS, and septic-like circulatory collapse.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, daily quotidian fever, 24-hour cycle, knowlesi fever rhythm, quotidian paroxysm
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as daily quotidian fever attacks in human infections with the simian parasite P. knowlesi, differentiating it chronologically from the 48- or 72-hour periodicities of other human species.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, quartan malarial nephropathy, Plasmodium malariae, nephrotic syndrome, proteinuria
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as quartan malarial nephropathy in long-standing P. malariae infection, presenting with heavy proteinuria, generalized edema, and steroid-resistant membrano-proliferative glomerulonephritis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, immune complex glomerulonephritis, glomerular deposition, complement activation, hematuria
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as immune complex glomerulonephritis secondary to chronic low-grade parasitemia, leading to subacute nephrotic syndrome and progressive glomerulosclerosis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, generalized convulsions, seizures, tonic-clonic, cerebral malaria, pediatric seizures
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as generalized convulsions occurring repetitively in children and adults with cerebral malaria, requiring parenteral anticonvulsants and airway protection.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, unarousable coma, encephalopathy, Glasgow coma score, Blantyre coma score, consciousness
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as unarousable coma with loss of meaningful purposeful motor response to painful stimuli, serving as the cardinal definition of cerebral malaria.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, prostration, severe weakness, inability to sit, exhaustion, danger sign
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as prostration defined by extreme neuromuscular exhaustion and inability to feed or sit unsupported, signifying severe systemic malaria requiring immediate parenteral treatment.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, acidotic breathing, Kussmaul respiration, air hunger, hyperventilation, lactic acidosis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as acidotic Kussmaul breathing characterized by deep sighs, sustained tachypnea, and chest indrawing driven by medullary chemoreceptor stimulation from systemic lactic acidosis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, persistent vomiting, intractable emesis, inability to retain oral intake, oral intolerance
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as persistent vomiting preventing oral fluid and drug intake, mandating immediate transition to parenteral antimalarial therapy.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, macroscopic hemoglobinuria, dark urine, intravascular hemolysis, blackwater fever
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as macroscopic hemoglobinuria where acute intravascular hemolysis saturates circulating haptoglobin, allowing free hemoglobin to filter through glomeruli and precipitate in renal tubules.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, hemoglobinuric nephrosis, tubular necrosis, heme toxicity, casts, acute renal failure
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as malarial hemoglobinuric nephrosis resulting from toxic heme iron release, lipid peroxidation, and tubular obstruction during severe intravascular hemolytic crises.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, microvascular sequestration, cytoadherence, PfEMP1, capillary plugging, tissue ischemia
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as microvascular erythrocyte sequestration where PfEMP1-mediated endothelial cytoadherence occludes capillary lumens in the brain, kidneys, intestines, and lungs, creating localized microvascular hypoxia.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, secondary bacteremia, Salmonella, bacterial co-infection, gut barrier breach, sepsis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as secondary bacterial bacteremia, most commonly with non-typhoidal Salmonella species, promoted by intestinal mucosal ischemia and impaired neutrophil and macrophage function during acute malaria.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, malarial paroxysm, rigors, fever spike, diaphoresis, schizont rupture
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Features the classic malarial paroxysm, a pathognomonic clinical sequence of shaking cold rigors followed by burning hot hyperpyrexia and concluding with profuse defervescing diaphoresis.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, cold stage, teeth-chattering rigors, shivering, piloerection, cyanosis
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Features the paroxysm cold stage lasting 15 to 60 minutes, characterized by intense teeth-chattering rigors, shivering, gooseflesh (cutis anserina), and peripheral cyanosis.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, hot stage, hyperpyrexia, dry burning skin, throbbing headache, delirium
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Features the paroxysm hot stage lasting 2 to 6 hours, characterized by sudden soaring body temperatures (39-41°C), intensely flushed dry skin, throbbing headache, and extreme restlessness.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, sweating stage, drenching diaphoresis, defervescence, exhaustion, relief
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Features the paroxysm sweating stage lasting 2 to 4 hours, marked by drenching generalized diaphoresis, rapid normalization of body temperature, and profound physical exhaustion.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, tertian fever, 48-hour periodicity, vivax, ovale, falciparum, schizogony
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Features tertian fever periodicity occurring every 48 hours in Plasmodium vivax, Plasmodium ovale, and synchronized Plasmodium falciparum infections, synchronizing with the 48-hour erythrocytic schizogony cycle.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, quartan fever, 72-hour periodicity, Plasmodium malariae, synchronized cycle
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Features quartan fever periodicity recurring precisely every 72 hours in Plasmodium malariae infections, matching its prolonged 72-hour intraerythrocytic development cycle.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, quotidian fever, 24-hour periodicity, Plasmodium knowlesi, rapid replication
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Features quotidian fever periodicity recurring every 24 hours in Plasmodium knowlesi infections, matching its accelerated 24-hour intraerythrocytic schizogonic lifespan.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, tender splenomegaly, splenic enlargement, acute congestion, red pulp hyperplasia
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Elicits palpable tender splenomegaly on abdominal palpation, emerging within 3 to 7 days of acute illness due to acute splenic congestion and clearance of parasitized red blood cells.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, soft splenomegaly, splenic palpation, acute congestion, friable spleen
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Presents with soft, easily compressible splenic enlargement with a palpable lower pole below the left costal margin, distinct from the rock-hard splenomegaly of chronic myeloproliferative disorders.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, scleral icterus, jaundice, unconjugated bilirubin, hemolytic icterus
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Displays visible scleral icterus reflecting elevated unconjugated serum bilirubin generated by ongoing intravascular and reticuloendothelial erythrocyte destruction.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, mucocutaneous pallor, severe anemia, acute hemolysis, pale skin
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates marked mucocutaneous pallor affecting the lips, tongue, and nail beds, serving as a rapid visual indicator of acute hemolytic hemoglobin drop.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, palmar pallor, palmar creases, pediatric triage, severe malarial anemia
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates prominent palmar pallor (whitening of palmar skin and creases), serving as a validated bedside screening sign for severe malarial anemia in children.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, conjunctival pallor, palpebral conjunctiva, bedside screening, anemia sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Exhibits severe conjunctival rim pallor on lower eyelid eversion, correlating clinically with hemoglobin levels falling below 7 to 8 g/dL.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, retinal whitening, malarial retinopathy, macular opacification, capillary arrest
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Shows retinal whitening on dilated funduscopy, characterized by patchy, pale opacification of the macula and perimacular retina resulting from local microvascular capillary arrest.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, vessel discoloration, orange vessels, white capillaries, cytoadherence
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Displays retinal vessel discoloration where retinal capillaries and venules appear abnormally orange or white due to packed sequestered non-perfusing erythrocyte columns.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, retinal hemorrhages, blot hemorrhages, posterior pole, microvascular rupture
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Exhibits intraretinal blot hemorrhages and white-centered hemorrhages across the posterior pole on direct or indirect ophthalmoscopic examination.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, Roth spots, pale-centered hemorrhages, funduscopy, capillary microthrombosis
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates pale-centered retinal hemorrhages (Roth spots) resulting from localized retinal capillary thrombosis and endothelial rupture during hyperparasitemia.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, Blantyre coma score, pediatric coma, cerebral malaria, motor score, verbal score
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates a Blantyre Coma Score below 3 in pediatric patients, confirming unarousable coma and defining the presence of cerebral malaria.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, Glasgow coma scale, low GCS, adult cerebral malaria, neurological depression
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates a Glasgow Coma Scale score below 11 in adults, identifying severe cerebral impairment and guiding urgent parenteral antimalarial therapy.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, hyperpyrexia, temperature over 40C, core hyperthermia, extreme fever spike
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Records core hyperpyrexia exceeding 40°C on clinical thermometry during the acme of the paroxysm hot phase.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, tender hepatomegaly, liver enlargement, hepatic congestion, right upper quadrant
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Elicits a soft, smooth, tender liver edge palpable 2 to 4 cm below the right costal margin reflecting acute hepatic vascular congestion and Kupffer cell hyperplasia.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, peripheral vasoconstriction, cutis anserina, acral cyanosis, cold extremities
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates marked peripheral vasoconstriction with cool dusky digits and goosebumps during the initial cold phase of the paroxysm.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, cold clammy skin, shock extremities, peripheral hypoperfusion, algid collapse
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Exhibits cold, clammy distal extremities and cyanotic acral beds in patients evolving into algid malaria or decompensated circulatory shock.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, capillary refill time, prolonged refill, microcirculatory pooling, hypoperfusion
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates prolonged capillary refill time exceeding 3 seconds on the nail bed or sternum, reflecting severe peripheral hypoperfusion and systemic microvascular pooling.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, acidotic hyperventilation, Kussmaul sign, rapid deep breathing, acidosis sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Exhibits rapid, deep, non-obstructive respiratory movements without focal pulmonary consolidation, signaling systemic lactic acidosis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, pulmonary crackles, bibasilar rales, pulmonary edema, lung auscultation
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Detects fine inspiratory bibasilar crackles on chest auscultation, indicating early pulmonary capillary fluid transudation or non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, postural hypotension, orthostasis, volume depletion, vasodilatation, tachycardia
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Elicits orthostatic drop in blood pressure accompanied by postural lightheadedness and tachycardia secondary to acute dehydration, high fever, and peripheral vasodilatation.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, absence of lymphadenopathy, normal lymph nodes, differential sign, no adenopathy
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Consistently exhibits an absence of significant localized or generalized lymphadenopathy, helping differentiate malaria from acute rickettsial illnesses or infectious mononucleosis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, thick blood smear, Giemsa stain, high sensitivity, parasite screening
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Detects intraerythrocytic Plasmodium parasites on thick Giemsa-stained blood smear at triage, providing high-sensitivity screening (limit of detection 10-50 parasites/µL).

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, thin blood smear, species differentiation, parasitemia quantification, morphology
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates morphological speciation and precise percentage parasitemia quantification on methanol-fixed thin Giemsa blood smear.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, ring forms, early trophozoites, intraerythrocytic, Giemsa, chromatin dot
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Displays delicate intraerythrocytic ring-form trophozoites featuring a thin blue cytoplasmic circle and red chromatin dot inside normal-sized or enlarged erythrocytes.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, falciparum gametocytes, banana-shaped, crescentic, sexual stages, Giemsa
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Identifies diagnostic crescent- or banana-shaped sexual gametocytes on peripheral thin smear, confirming Plasmodium falciparum infection.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, amoeboid trophozoites, vivax morphology, enlarged red cells, Giemsa
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Reveals pleomorphic amoeboid trophozoites within enlarged, pale erythrocytes characteristic of Plasmodium vivax infection.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, Schuffner dots, erythrocyte stippling, vivax, ovale, Giemsa smear
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates fine pink/red stippling (Schüffner dots) throughout the cytoplasm of parasitized enlarged erythrocytes in P. vivax and P. ovale infections.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, malariae band forms, ribbon-like, senescent erythrocytes, quartan malaria
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Shows characteristic equatorial band-shaped trophozoites spanning across the diameter of normal-sized senescent red blood cells in Plasmodium malariae infection.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, knowlesi morphology, band forms, hyperparasitemia, simian malaria
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Detects band-form trophozoites resembling P. malariae but accompanied by high-density ring-form parasitemia resembling P. falciparum, pathognomonic for Plasmodium knowlesi.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, PfHRP2, rapid diagnostic test, falciparum antigen, immunochromatography
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Yields positive result on rapid immunochromatographic diagnostic strip for Plasmodium falciparum Histidine-Rich Protein 2 (PfHRP2) antigen within 15 minutes.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, pan-pLDH, parasite lactate dehydrogenase, pan-Plasmodium antigen, viability marker
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Tests positive for pan-Plasmodium parasite lactate dehydrogenase (pLDH), verifying active metabolic parasite turnover and discriminating vivax/malariae/ovale from past falciparum antigenemia.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, aldolase antigen, pan-Plasmodium, glycolytic enzyme, rapid test strip
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Tests positive for pan-Plasmodium aldolase enzyme on combination immunochromatographic rapid test cassettes.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, HRP2 gene deletion, diagnostic escape, false negative RDT, pfhrp2 deletion
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Exhibits false-negative PfHRP2 RDT results despite patent parasitemia on microscopy due to emerging pfhrp2 and pfhrp3 chromosomal gene deletions.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, indirect bilirubin, hemolysis, liver function
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Displays predominant unconjugated (indirect) hyperbilirubinemia (> 2.0 mg/dL) with normal or only slightly elevated direct bilirubin, reflecting accelerated hemoglobin breakdown.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, depleted haptoglobin, undetectable haptoglobin, intravascular hemolysis marker
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Reveals profoundly depleted or undetectable serum haptoglobin (< 0.1 g/L) due to rapid binding and clearance of free intravascular hemoglobin.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, elevated LDH, lactate dehydrogenase, hemolysis hallmark, red cell lysis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Shows marked elevation of serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH > 500-1500 IU/L), serving as a sensitive surrogate marker for ongoing erythrocyte lysis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, marked thrombocytopenia, platelets under 100000, splenic pooling, admission CBC
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates marked thrombocytopenia (platelet count < 100,000/µL) on admission automated CBC in 70-85% of acute malaria cases.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, profound thrombocytopenia, platelets under 50000, immune destruction, bleeding risk
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Exhibits profound thrombocytopenia (platelet count < 50,000/µL) driven by intense splenic platelet pooling, macrophage activation, and immune destruction.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, normal leukocyte count, normal WBC, absence of leukocytosis, admission CBC
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Maintains a normal white blood cell count (4,000 to 10,000/µL) in uncomplicated malaria, contrasting sharply with pyogenic bacterial infections.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, leukopenia, low WBC, splenic margination, admission complete blood count
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates absolute leukopenia (WBC < 4,000/µL) during the acute fever paroxysm, secondary to splenic margination and bone marrow suppression.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, hyperparasitemia, parasitemia over 2 percent, non-immune traveler, thin smear
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates peripheral blood parasitemia exceeding 2% infected erythrocytes on thin film, indicating severe disease in non-immune travelers.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, hyperparasitemia, parasitemia over 10 percent, severe criteria, WHO definition
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Quantifies parasitemia exceeding 10% infected erythrocytes on thin film, qualifying as severe malaria irrespective of host immune status.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, parasitemia over 100000, quantitative parasite count, high density, severe threshold
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates absolute asexual parasite count exceeding 100,000 parasites/µL of blood, identifying hyperparasitemic malaria with high microvascular burden.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, elevated lactate, plasma lactate over 5 mmol/L, lactic acidosis, tissue hypoxia
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Measures elevated venous or arterial plasma lactate exceeding 5.0 mmol/L, identifying severe metabolic lactic acidosis and tissue hypoxia.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, base deficit, blood gas analysis, metabolic acidosis, acid-base status
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Exhibits an elevated base deficit exceeding 10 mEq/L on admission arterial or venous blood gas analysis in complicated malaria.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, low bicarbonate, bicarbonate under 15 mmol/L, metabolic acidosis, acidemia
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates reduced serum bicarbonate (< 15 mmol/L) secondary to unmeasured organic acid accumulation and microvascular hypoperfusion.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, low blood glucose, hypoglycemia under 2.2 mmol/L, bedside glucometry
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Records blood glucose level below 2.2 mmol/L (40 mg/dL) on bedside glucometer or admission laboratory testing.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, elevated creatinine, creatinine over 3 mg/dL, acute kidney injury, renal chemistry
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates acute elevation of serum creatinine > 3.0 mg/dL (265 µmol/L), establishing acute renal impairment.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, elevated blood urea, BUN, azotemia, renal hypoperfusion, catabolism
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Shows markedly elevated blood urea nitrogen (BUN > 20 mmol/L) with disproportionate azotemia from muscle catabolism and renal hypoperfusion.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, dark mahogany urine, port-wine urine, visual inspection, hemoglobinuria, blackwater
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Produces macroscopic dark mahogany, dark red, or black urine on visual inspection in patients experiencing acute hemoglobinuria.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, dipstick positive, absent RBCs, free hemoglobin, urinalysis, sediment
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Yields strongly positive urine dipstick for blood with microscopic absence of intact red blood cells on sediment examination, confirming free hemoglobinuria.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, normocytic anemia, normochromic, hematocrit drop, complete blood count
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Reveals normocytic normochromic anemia with rapid drop in hemoglobin and hematocrit from baseline on serial complete blood counts.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, reticulocytosis, reticulocyte count, bone marrow response, erythropoiesis recovery
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates elevated reticulocyte production index (> 2.0%) emerging 3 to 7 days post-paroxysm as bone marrow recovers from cytokine inhibition.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, mild transaminitis, AST elevation, ALT elevation, liver enzymes, preserved synthetic
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Shows modest elevation of AST and ALT (typically 1.5 to 3 times upper limit of normal), with preservation of normal hepatocellular architecture.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, normal PT, normal fibrinogen, absence of DIC, isolated thrombocytopenia
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Shows thrombocytopenia accompanied by normal or minimally prolonged prothrombin time (PT) and normal fibrinogen levels, ruling out overt consumable coagulopathy.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, POCUS splenomegaly, splenic length over 12 cm, ultrasound, homogeneous spleen
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Demonstrates enlarged splenic bipolar length (> 12 cm in adults) with homogeneous parenchymal echotexture on bedside ultrasound.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, POCUS gallbladder, thin wall under 3 mm, no edema, distinguishes from dengue
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Reveals a thin, non-edematous gallbladder wall (< 3 mm) without pericholecystic fluid, helping exclude acute dengue plasma leakage.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, POCUS no ascites, absent pleural effusion, no third-space fluid, ultrasound negative
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Demonstrates complete absence of third-space plasma extravasation (no pleural effusions, no ascites) on rapid abdominal and thoracic ultrasound windows.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, chest radiograph, clear lungs, no infiltrates, initial CXR, baseline imaging
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Shows clear lung fields without focal infiltrates or effusions on initial chest radiograph in uncomplicated malaria.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, Anopheles mosquito, vector bite, sporozoite inoculation, primary transmission
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Contracted via the bite of an infected female mosquito of the genus Anopheles injecting motile Plasmodium sporozoites into subcutaneous tissue and bloodstream.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, nocturnal biting, dusk to dawn, vector behavior, sleeping outdoors, bed nets
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Associated with exposure to nocturnal mosquito biting activity occurring predominantly between dusk and dawn, the peak foraging period of Anopheles vectors.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, tropical travel, endemic travel, travel history, geographic exposure
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Acquired during travel to or residence in malaria-endemic tropical and subtropical latitudes of Africa, Asia, and Latin America.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, sub-Saharan Africa, high transmission, falciparum predominance, travel medicine
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Linked to travel in sub-Saharan Africa, which accounts for >95% of global malaria infections and mortality, predominantly driven by virulent Plasmodium falciparum.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, Southeast Asia travel, forest travel, knowlesi reservoir, vivax transmission
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Acquired during travel to forested or fringe areas of Southeast Asia where Plasmodium vivax and zoonotic Plasmodium knowlesi predominate.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, Amazon basin travel, South America, vivax predominance, gold mining camps
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Linked to travel within the Amazon Basin and lowlands of South America, where Plasmodium vivax accounts for the majority of clinical cases.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, lack of chemoprophylaxis, non-adherence, atovaquone-proguanil, doxycycline, mefloquine
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Preceded by absence of, non-adherence to, or inappropriate choice of pharmacological antimalarial chemoprophylaxis during endemic exposure.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, non-immune traveler, expatriates, lack of premunition, severe malaria risk
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Displays heightened susceptibility to rapid severe falciparum complications in non-immune travelers and expatriates lacking acquired semi-protective humoral immunity.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, children under five, pediatric vulnerability, high mortality, severe anemia risk
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Affects children under five years of age as a high-risk host group, accounting for approximately 75% of all global malaria mortalities due to lack of acquired immunity.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, pregnant women, primigravida, placental sequestration, severe maternal anemia
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Selectively targets pregnant women (especially primigravidae and secundigravidae) who suffer severe anemia, hypoglycemia, cerebral malaria, and placental sequestration.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, HIV co-infection, immunosuppression, CD4 depletion, higher parasitemia
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Exacerbates parasitemia density and severe clinical endpoints in patients living with HIV/AIDS due to impaired cell-mediated and humoral parasite control.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, asplenic patients, splenectomy, hyposplenism, overwhelming parasitemia
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Precipitates fulminant hyperparasitemia and rapid death in surgically asplenic or functionally hyposplenic patients lacking splenic parasite-clearance capacity.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, blood transfusion, transfusion-transmitted malaria, donor screening, parenteral
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Transmitted parenterally via transfusion of parasitized donor red blood cells, which directly establishes erythrocytic infection without a hepatic pre-erythrocytic phase.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, needle sharing, intravenous drug use, parenteral inoculation, bloodborne spread
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Transmitted parenterally through shared contaminated hypodermic needles among intravenous drug users.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, congenital transmission, vertical transmission, transplacental, newborn infection
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Transmitted vertically from mother to fetus via transplacental microscopic hemorrhage or during delivery.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, falciparum incubation, 9 to 14 days, pre-erythrocytic schizogony, symptom onset
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Exhibits an incubation period of 9 to 14 days (typically 10 to 12 days) for Plasmodium falciparum from sporozoite inoculation to initial symptom onset.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, minimum incubation, 7 days threshold, liver stage schizogony, biological rule
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Requires an obligatory minimum biological hepatic pre-erythrocytic schizogony period of 7 days before falciparum merozoites can enter the blood and trigger fever.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, vivax incubation, 12 to 18 days, primary attack, hepatic development
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Manifests an initial incubation period of 12 to 18 days for primary Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium ovale attacks.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, vivax delayed latency, 8 to 10 months, hibernans phenotype, temperate strain
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Exhibits delayed-latency incubation of 8 to 10 months (and up to 2 years) in temperate strains of Plasmodium vivax (such as P. vivax hibernans).

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, hypnozoites, liver stage dormancy, vivax relapse, ovale relapse, radical cure
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Sustains late clinical relapses weeks to months after primary infection due to dormant hepatic hypnozoites of P. vivax and P. ovale.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, ovale incubation, 15 to 18 days, pre-erythrocytic phase, tertian paroxysm
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Demonstrates an incubation period of 15 to 18 days for Plasmodium ovale, with potential for dormant hypnozoite relapses.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, malariae incubation, 18 to 40 days, extended incubation, quartan malaria
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Features a prolonged incubation period of 18 to 40 days for Plasmodium malariae, with capacity for low-grade persistence spanning decades.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, knowlesi incubation, 9 to 12 days, zoonotic incubation, macaque reservoir
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Displays an incubation period of 9 to 12 days following transmission of zoonotic Plasmodium knowlesi sporozoites from monkey reservoirs.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, Anopheles stephensi, urban malaria, invasive vector, artificial containers
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Transmitted in emerging urban contexts through invasive Anopheles stephensi vectors capable of breeding in artificial domestic clean-water containers.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, negative blood smears, serial microscopy, three negative films, exclusion criterion
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out by three consecutive quality-assured thick and thin Giemsa blood smears obtained 12 to 24 hours apart yielding zero visible parasites.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, onset under 7 days, incubation boundary, minimum pre-erythrocytic phase, rules out
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out when fever onset occurs less than 7 days after the very first potential exposure in a malaria-endemic region, violating the minimum hepatic schizogony period.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, plasma leakage, hemoconcentration, hematocrit rise, ascites, pleural effusion, dengue
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out as uncomplicated malaria by the presence of marked microvascular plasma leakage, severe hemoconcentration (hematocrit rise >= 20%), or pleural effusions.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, marked leukocytosis, WBC over 15000, neutrophilia, left shift, pyogenic infection
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out by marked neutrophilic leukocytosis exceeding 15,000/µL with bandemia and toxic granulation, which strongly points to bacterial sepsis or leptospirosis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, cutaneous eschar, necrotic ulcer, scrub typhus, spotted fever, chigger bite
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out by the presence of a painless cigarette-burn cutaneous necrotic eschar surrounded by an erythematous halo, pathognomonic for scrub typhus or spotted fevers.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, regional lymphadenopathy, tender bubo, lymph node enlargement, rickettsial sign
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out by the presence of prominent tender localized or regional lymphadenopathy, which is absent in malaria and indicates rickettsioses, plague, or tularemia.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, maculopapular rash, diffuse exanthem, petechial rash, viral exanthem, rules out
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out by an extensive erythematous maculopapular, petechial, or purpuric exanthem, which is absent in malaria and indicates dengue, measles, or meningococcemia.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, transaminases over 1000, AST over 1000, ALT over 1000, hepatic necrosis, viral hepatitis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out by massive serum transaminase elevations (AST and ALT > 1,000 U/L), which points decisively to acute viral hepatitis or toxic liver necrosis rather than malarial hepatopathy.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, conjunctival suffusion, red eyes without discharge, leptospirosis hallmark, rules out
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out by striking bilateral ciliary conjunctival suffusion without purulent exudate, which is characteristic of leptospirosis rather than malaria.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, lobar consolidation, air bronchograms, bacterial pneumonia, chest x-ray, focal infiltrate
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out by dense focal lobar consolidation with air bronchograms on chest radiography, indicating primary bacterial pneumonia.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, purulent CSF, CSF pleocytosis, bacterial meningitis, low CSF glucose, elevated protein
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out by purulent CSF pleocytosis (> 100 WBC/µL, predominantly neutrophils) with low glucose and elevated protein, confirming pyogenic bacterial meningitis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exudative tonsillitis, pharyngeal exudate, streptococcal pharyngitis, sore throat
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out by the presence of tonsillopharyngeal exudates, palatal petechiae, and anterior cervical adenitis, indicating bacterial or viral pharyngitis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, pyuria, bacteriuria, urinary tract infection, positive leukocyte esterase, nitrites
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out by significant pyuria (> 10 WBC/HPF) accompanied by visible bacteriuria and positive leukocyte esterase/nitrites on urinalysis, indicating urinary tract infection.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, peritonitis, board-like abdomen, involuntary guarding, visceral perforation, surgical abdomen
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out by generalized abdominal muscular rigidity, involuntary guarding, and rebound tenderness without splenomegaly, indicating acute gastrointestinal hollow viscous perforation.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, direct hyperbilirubinemia, conjugated jaundice, cholestasis, biliary obstruction
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out by isolated conjugated (direct) hyperbilirubinemia with high alkaline phosphatase and acholic stools, indicating obstructive extrahepatic cholestasis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, acholic stools, pale stools, biliary obstruction, extrahepatic cholestasis, rules out
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out by clay-colored acholic stools and dark urine without hemolysis, which establishes mechanical biliary obstruction rather than hemolytic malaria.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, stepladder fever, relative bradycardia, Faget sign, typhoid fever, absence of rigors
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out by insidious daily step-ladder temperature escalation associated with relative bradycardia (Faget sign) and absence of rigors, typical of typhoid fever.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, beta-lactam response, antibiotic defervescence, intrinsic resistance, bacterial cure
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out by prompt clinical defervescence and symptom resolution following exclusive beta-lactam antibiotic therapy, to which Plasmodium species are intrinsically impervious.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, no endemic exposure, zero travel history, non-endemic, no transfusion, rules out
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out in patients with zero lifetime or recent travel to endemic regions, no history of blood transfusion, and no needle sharing or airport vector exposure.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, normal platelet count, platelets over 200000, lack of thrombocytopenia, rules out
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out in acute high-grade febrile presentations when platelet counts remain persistently normal (> 200,000/µL) across serial measurements, as malaria almost uniformly lowers platelet counts.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, severe hypofibrinogenemia, fibrinogen under 100, consumable coagulopathy, severe DIC
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out as uncomplicated or standard severe malaria by severe hypofibrinogenemia (< 100 mg/dL) with mark-prolonged PT/PTT at admission, indicating acute consumable DIC from bacterial sepsis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, splenic abscess, focal splenic lesion, cystic cavity, ultrasound finding, pyogenic
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ruled out by bedside ultrasonography revealing thick-walled splenic cystic cavities with internal gas or fluid debris, establishing pyogenic splenic abscess.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Dengue fever, retro-orbital pain, plasma leakage, hemoconcentration, tourniquet test
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Dengue Fever, which features retro-orbital headache, positive tourniquet test, hemoconcentration (hematocrit rise >= 20%), pleural effusions, and AST > ALT elevation without early splenomegaly; in contrast, Malaria features hemolytic anemia, unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, early splenomegaly, and intraerythrocytic parasites on blood smear.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Typhoid fever, Salmonella Typhi, stepladder fever, Faget sign, rose spots
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Typhoid Fever, which presents with an insidious step-ladder temperature rise, relative bradycardia (Faget sign), rose spots on the trunk, and dull apathetic facies; in contrast, Malaria presents with abrupt violent shaking rigors, drenching diaphoresis, acute hemolytic anemia, and rapid defervescence cycles.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Leptospirosis, conjunctival suffusion, calf tenderness, direct bilirubin, leukocytosis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Leptospirosis, which presents with striking bilateral conjunctival suffusion without discharge, severe gastrocnemius calf tenderness, marked neutrophilic leukocytosis, and direct hyperbilirubinemia; in contrast, Malaria exhibits indirect hyperbilirubinemia, normal or low WBC count, and intraerythrocytic ring forms.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Scrub typhus, Orientia tsutsugamushi, eschar, regional adenopathy, chigger
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Scrub Typhus, which features a pathognomonic necrotic black eschar at the chigger bite site, regional lymphadenopathy, and macular trunk rash; in contrast, Malaria lacks eschars and rash, and is diagnosed by intraerythrocytic ring forms and positive HRP2/pLDH antigen tests.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Babesiosis, Babesia microti, Maltese cross, tick bite, negative RDT, temperate zone
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Babesiosis, which also causes intraerythrocytic rings and hemolysis but is transmitted by Ixodes ticks in temperate North America/Europe, displays pathognomonic tetrad Maltese cross forms without hemozoin pigment, and tests negative on malaria rapid antigen tests.
