relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, African trypanosomiasis, sleeping sickness, chancre, Winterbottom sign, tsetse fly
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from African Trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness), which is transmitted by tsetse flies, presents with an indurated trypanosomal chancre, posterior cervical lymphadenopathy (Winterbottom sign), and daytime somnolence with trypomastigotes in blood; in contrast, Malaria lacks trypanosomal chancres and presents with intraerythrocytic Plasmodium trophozoites.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Visceral leishmaniasis, Kala-azar, massive splenomegaly, pancytopenia, LD bodies
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Visceral Leishmaniasis (Kala-azar), which runs a subacute or chronic course over months with massive firm splenomegaly, hypergammaglobulinemia, profound wasting, and intracellular Leishmania amastigotes (LD bodies) in bone marrow; in contrast, Malaria causes acute fever paroxysms, rapid hemolysis, and responds to antimalarials.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Yellow fever, viral hemorrhagic fever, black vomit, extreme transaminitis, Faget sign
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Yellow Fever, which causes a biphasic fever with mid-stage remission, severe hepatocellular jaundice with transaminases in the thousands, early Faget sign, and hematemesis (black vomit); in contrast, Malaria exhibits modest transaminitis (< 3x ULN), predominant indirect hyperbilirubinemia, and responds to intravenous artesunate.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, acute viral hepatitis, hepatitis A, transaminases over 1000, direct hyperbilirubinemia
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Acute Viral Hepatitis, which presents with marked direct hyperbilirubinemia, severe anorexia, dark urine with acholic stools, and extreme transaminitis (ALT/AST > 1,000 U/L); in contrast, Malaria exhibits predominantly unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, mild transaminase elevation, acute thrombocytopenia, and blood smear parasitemia.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Meningococcal meningitis, Neisseria meningitidis, nuchal rigidity, purpuric rash, CSF
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Meningococcal Meningitis, which presents with prominent nuchal rigidity, positive Kernig/Brudzinski signs, purpuric/petechial skin rash, and purulent CSF with Gram-negative diplococci; in contrast, Cerebral Malaria presents with unarousable coma without purulent CSF pleocytosis, accompanied by malarial retinopathy and peripheral parasitemia.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, bacterial sepsis, bacteremia, neutrophilic leukocytosis, procalcitonin, blood cultures
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Bacterial Sepsis, which characteristically demonstrates marked neutrophilic leukocytosis with significant left shift, elevated procalcitonin, and identifiable primary pyogenic focus; in contrast, Malaria typically shows normal or low WBC count, negative blood cultures, and positive Giemsa microscopy.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Influenza infection, orthomyxovirus, coryza, cough, sore throat, lack of hemolysis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Influenza Infection, which is characterized by prominent upper and lower respiratory symptoms including dry cough, sore throat, coryza, and substernal burning; in contrast, uncomplicated Malaria lacks prominent rhinorrhea and pharyngitis, presenting instead with splenomegaly, hemolytic anemia, and travel history.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Chikungunya virus, severe polyarthralgia, small joint arthritis, tenosynovitis, rash
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Chikungunya Virus, which presents with incapacitating, symmetrical, bilateral polyarthralgias and polyarthritis primarily affecting small joints of hands and feet, often accompanied by maculopapular rash; in contrast, Malaria causes generalized myalgias and backache without inflammatory joint synovitis.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Relapsing fever borreliosis, Borrelia recurrentis, spirochetemia, prolonged fever, louse
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Relapsing Fever Borreliosis (louse-borne or tick-borne), which produces high continuous fevers lasting 3 to 7 days followed by afebrile intervals of several days and displays extracellular spirochetes on darkfield or Giemsa blood smear; in contrast, Malaria exhibits intraerythrocytic parasites and shorter 24- to 72-hour paroxysms.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Q fever, Coxiella burnetii, livestock exposure, doughnut granulomas, atypical pneumonia
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from acute Q Fever (Coxiella burnetii), which is transmitted via inhalation of barnyard dust or contact with livestock products and manifests as acute pneumonia with cough or granulomatous hepatitis; in contrast, Malaria involves mosquito transmission and intraerythrocytic parasitism.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, acute HIV seroconversion, viral exanthem, mucosal ulcerations, lymphadenopathy, pharyngitis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Acute HIV Seroconversion syndrome, which presents with symmetrical generalized lymphadenopathy, painful mucocutaneous ulcerations, pharyngitis, and diffuse erythematous morbilliform rash; in contrast, Malaria exhibits splenomegaly, hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, and intraerythrocytic parasites without pharyngitis or mucosal ulcers.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Human granulocytic anaplasmosis, Anaplasma phagocytophilum, neutrophil morulae, tick
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Human Granulocytic Anaplasmosis, which is transmitted by Ixodes ticks, presents with intracytoplasmic morulae inside peripheral neutrophils, and responds to doxycycline; in contrast, Malaria is transmitted by Anopheles mosquitoes, infects erythrocytes, and responds to artemisinin-based regimens.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Amebic liver abscess, Entamoeba histolytica, liver abscess, anchovy paste, ultrasound
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Amebic Liver Abscess, which presents with persistent right upper quadrant pain, point tenderness over intercostal spaces, solitary liver fluid collection on ultrasound ('anchovy paste' aspirate), and high leukocytosis; in contrast, Malaria shows diffuse hepatosplenomegaly without focal hepatic abscess cavities.
